chapter: Harry Parker's, the district and its characters
title: Joe Oliver's band at Hunts and Nagel's, and a great clarinetist
summary: Allen asks about Abadie's and other joints; Dawson says Joe Oliver had a full band with Louis Keppard, Pop Foster and Willie Foster, then tries to recall a clarinet and sax player who could read anything.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Who were the great clarinetists? Favorites and rivals

blocks.x: What about Abadese? Did you ever go by Abadese? Down there, I figured it was on the anvil. Well, it had another name and I can't remember. Something like the, the Princeton Inn or the Princeton Club or something like that. No, Joe Oliver used to be there with Big Eye Louie and Ernest Rogers and Wooden Joe was in there playing clarinet. Yeah. You know the place. That was the Magnolia band. No, I think Richard M. Jones was there. Not the Magnolia. Not the band that was on Hunts and Nagels, but another one. This is a four piece. Papa Selle's back. No, it's a four piece band with Joe

Olavon and Wooden Joe. Yeah, well, no, he had a whole band. Oh yeah, he had a whole band? Joe Oliver had a whole band. Mm-hm. Celestane. Joe Oliver had, he had Louis Kepard on the guitar, Pop Foster on the bass, and Willie Foster on the violin. That was Pop Foster's brother. And, uh, that's the, uh, the famous clarin, uh, clarinet and saxophone, uh, hot dog.
Where did he die? The clarinet play, is that the one that went up north or stayed here?

Oh, that fellow, that fellow was a famous musician. Was he from a musical family, or? He from, he from, he didn't have much, much kin, folks there, but he was a great, great, great saxophone and clarinet. Uh, yeah, but I'm trying to think of what he did, no. Could he read much, or? Could he? Ha! Sight reader. A man could read. If he hear a number playin, and he had a shirt with a cuff on it, he, he, he, he'd ride it all right, right on his cuff. Was he as good as Bichet, or T.O., or any of those people? Well, yeah, he was better. Better than T.O. and Bichet? Yeah, Bichet was good, yeah, but he was better. Was he better than T.O.? Just about the same. Same grade. MacCurdy? Was he as good as MacCurdy? Charlie, uh, Charlie MacCurdy? That's the one I'm talkin' about. Oh, you're talkin' about Charlie? That's the one I'm talkin' about. Oh, yeah. That's the man I'm talkin' about. I couldn't think of his name. He was the best. Where did he go? He left here or I don't know. He died. He died here? I don't know whether he died here or not. I know he died, it's been so long. He died a long time. Yeah, he's been dead a long time. He was the best.
